scenario: [LTIM.14.2]: a field outside its range is a ComputationError of kind DOMAIN, and the activation is abandoned. One `F` fact per case, its fields in `Int` slots so nothing folds, each pumped on its own. Each case has its own rule, whose `where` is `f.id == N and <the call> != <a constant>`: for the other facts `f.id == N` is false and absorbs nothing to raise ([LNUL.4.2]), so each fact raises from one node, and each fault is its own fault fact ([LERR.9.2]). `trapped` logs each ComputationError's kind. The cases: `calendar.time` with month 13 (1), 2023-02-29, no day of 2023 (2), hour 24 (3), minute 60 (4), second 60 (5) and nanosecond 1 000 000 000 (6), and `calendar.date(2023, 2, 29)` (8), each `DOMAIN`, and their rules never fire. The control, 7, is 2024-02-29T23:59:59.999999999, every field at the top of its range in a leap year: `leap_day` fires and logs `built 7`. A runtime that wrapped a field into the next unit, skipped the calendar check, or raised another kind logs a `built` line or another kind. PATH PINNED: libds `adapter_ds_calendar_time` / `adapter_ds_calendar_date`'s range checks (`calendar_days`, rete/adapters.c) and Mercury `ds.chrono.ltim_14_2_time` / `ltim_14_2_date` (`ltim_14_2_day_in_range`).
rules_ds:
import calendar

schema F scope logical:
    id: Int key
    y: Int mutable
    mo: Int mutable
    d: Int mutable
    h: Int mutable
    mi: Int mutable
    s: Int mutable
    ns: Int mutable

rule month_13:
    F f where f.id == 1 and calendar.time(f.y, f.mo, f.d, f.h, f.mi, f.s, f.ns) != calendar.time(1970, 1, 1)
->
    log info "built 1"

rule not_a_day:
    F f where f.id == 2 and calendar.time(f.y, f.mo, f.d, f.h, f.mi, f.s, f.ns) != calendar.time(1970, 1, 1)
->
    log info "built 2"

rule hour_24:
    F f where f.id == 3 and calendar.time(f.y, f.mo, f.d, f.h, f.mi, f.s, f.ns) != calendar.time(1970, 1, 1)
->
    log info "built 3"

rule minute_60:
    F f where f.id == 4 and calendar.time(f.y, f.mo, f.d, f.h, f.mi, f.s, f.ns) != calendar.time(1970, 1, 1)
->
    log info "built 4"

rule second_60:
    F f where f.id == 5 and calendar.time(f.y, f.mo, f.d, f.h, f.mi, f.s, f.ns) != calendar.time(1970, 1, 1)
->
    log info "built 5"

rule nanosecond_1e9:
    F f where f.id == 6 and calendar.time(f.y, f.mo, f.d, f.h, f.mi, f.s, f.ns) != calendar.time(1970, 1, 1)
->
    log info "built 6"

rule leap_day:
    F f where f.id == 7 and calendar.time(f.y, f.mo, f.d, f.h, f.mi, f.s, f.ns) != calendar.time(1970, 1, 1)
->
    log info "built 7"

rule date_not_a_day:
    F f where f.id == 8 and calendar.date(f.y, f.mo, f.d) != calendar.date(1970, 1, 1)
->
    log info "built 8"

rule trapped:
    ComputationError c
->
    log info "{c.kind}"
